principle: When a user writes a capability, synthesize it via a 5-stage flow against the registries, with frontier-LLM prompts FILLING a registry-driven scaffold (the LLM proposes; the scaffold + tests + governance dispose). Every decision BRANCHES + is VERSIONED; the cheapest option is tried first; a dead-end leaf BACKTRACKS up and tries another branch; all branches (winners + losers) are kept with lineage (lossless). Engine: _repos/teleon/backend/src/teleon/synthesis/{intent_to_dag,synthesis_tree}.py. serves_truth=false.

stages.prompt: How can we make this work? Provide an outline, considering this context.
stages.gate: a ladder/capability is matched (else honest 'no match')

stages.prompt: Fill in the outline with concrete components.
stages.gate: every option is a real registry component

stages.prompt: Create a DAG of components and test each component.
stages.gate: each chosen node passes its component test; whole DAG passes

stages.prompt: 5W1H verification ladder per DAG / node / group.
stages.output: who/what/where/when/why/how answered per node + group + dag

stages.prompt: Is this the best way? Alternatives? Pros/cons?
stages.gate: the chosen path beats the considered alternatives on the user's PreferenceProfile

branching.version_id: path of decisions from the root
branching.on_dead_end: jump back up to the parent and try the next untried branch; keep the abandoned branch with lineage
